topics.title: Random Processes and Noise
topics.syllabus: Random Processes: Auto correlation and power spectral density, properties of white noise, filtering of random signals through LTI systems.

cards.title: Stationarity, autocorrelation and PSD
cards.bodyHtml: A process is wide-sense stationary if its mean is constant and its autocorrelation depends only on the lag τ\tauτ. Everything else in this topic assumes WSS, and the PSD is simply the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation (Wiener–Khinchine).

cards.bodyHtml: White noise has a flat two-sided PSD N0/2N_0/2N0​/2, so its autocorrelation is an impulse: samples at any two distinct instants are uncorrelated. Its total power is infinite, which is why it only ever appears after a filter.

topics.title: Analog Modulation
topics.syllabus: Analog Communications: Amplitude modulation and demodulation, angle modulation and demodulation, spectra of AM and FM, super heterodyne receivers.

cards.title: Conventional AM: power and efficiency
cards.bodyHtml: The carrier carries no information but takes most of the power — that is the whole story of AM. At the legal maximum μ=1\mu=1μ=1, two-thirds of the transmitted power is still in the carrier.
cards.pitfallHtml: μ>1\mu>1μ>1 over-modulates: the envelope crosses zero, phase reversal appears, and an envelope detector output is distorted — a coherent detector would still recover it.

cards.title: Angle modulation: FM and PM
cards.bodyHtml: In FM the instantaneous frequency follows the message; in PM the instantaneous phase does. Since phase is the integral of frequency, FM of m(t)m(t)m(t) is PM of ∫m\int m∫m — which is how a question about one can be converted into the other.
cards.pitfallHtml: Narrowband FM (β≪1\beta\ll1β≪1) has the same bandwidth 2fm2f_m2fm​ as AM. The noise advantage of FM only appears in the wideband case, and it is bought with bandwidth.

topics.title: Information Theory
topics.syllabus: Information Theory: Entropy, mutual information and channel capacity theorem.

cards.title: Entropy and mutual information
cards.bodyHtml: Entropy is the average bits per symbol a source truly needs. It is largest when all symbols are equally likely and zero when the source is deterministic — so any question asking to maximise HHH is answered by equiprobability.
cards.pitfallHtml: Use log⁡2\log_2log2​. A natural log gives nats and an answer off by ln⁡2=0.693\ln2=0.693ln2=0.693 — a very common and very avoidable error.

cards.bodyHtml: Shannon's theorem sets the ceiling: reliable transmission is possible at any rate below CCC and impossible above it. Bandwidth and SNR trade against each other, but not equally — capacity grows only logarithmically with power.

cards.title: Sampling, quantisation and PCM

cards.title: Matched filter and optimum detection
cards.bodyHtml: The matched filter maximises SNR at the sampling instant, and that maximum depends only on the pulse energy, not its shape. ML detection picks the nearest signal point when priors are equal; MAP weights by the priors.

cards.title: DPCM and delta modulation
cards.bodyHtml: Successive speech or video samples are strongly correlated, so encoding the prediction error instead of the sample needs fewer bits for the same quality. DPCM does that with a multi-bit quantiser; delta modulation is the one-bit limit of the same idea, which is why it needs a much higher sampling rate.
cards.pitfallHtml: Increasing Δ\DeltaΔ cures slope overload and worsens granular noise; decreasing it does the reverse. Any DM question asking for an "optimum" step size is asking where those two curves cross.

cards.title: Hamming codes and CRC
cards.bodyHtml: A Hamming code is the single-error-correcting code with the fewest parity bits: rrr parity bits address 2r−12^r-12r−1 positions, so n=2r−1n=2^r-1n=2r−1 and k=n−rk=n-rk=n−r. The syndrome read as a binary number is the position of the error.
cards.pitfallHtml: CRC arithmetic is modulo 2 — subtraction is XOR, with no borrows. Doing the long division with ordinary binary subtraction gives a wrong remainder every time.
